edges.relation: Multi-stream ILP requires sync points to split a single bitstream into multiple independent decode positions
Sync-point finding is a special case of FSM convergence: probes from N offsets converge to one valid decode state
Both use speculative parallel execution with validation: CSE validates convergence, OCC validates segment boundaries
Interleaved streams provide the virtual multi-stream structure needed for ILP decode within a single format stream
Virtual interleaving requires finding evenly-spaced sync points to create stream boundaries
Multi-symbol mega tables reduce per-symbol decode latency, changing the ILP calculation for optimal stream count
Both exploit temporal overlap of operations; overlap hides decode/copy latency, pipeline extends this to multi-stage
SIMD copy acceleration benefits the LZ77 reconstruction stage, helping balance the pipeline
SIMD copies are the primary operation whose latency is hidden by overlapping with the next decode
Both exploit statistical patterns: prediction uses most-common symbol, mega-table precomputes common symbol pairs
Both apply prediction at different granularities: symbol-level prediction vs block-level table prediction
Block prediction enables speculative next-block decode; OCC handles validation and retry when prediction fails
Bitvector probing is an accelerated implementation of the sync-point discovery algorithm
Bitvectors represent reachable state sets compactly, equivalent to convergence set membership tracking
OCC provides the thread-level parallelism framework; ILP provides within-thread parallelism for each segment
Pipeline benefits from block prediction: knowing next block's table enables earlier pipeline stage startup

bridge_chains.name: neuroscience_to_hardware_optimization
bridge_chains.description: From neuroscience's predictive coding through data structure design to hardware-aware execution optimization. Each step reduces effective decode latency: prediction skips the most common case, mega-tables decode multiple symbols per lookup, ILP fills execution slots, and overlap hides remaining latency.

bridge_chains.name: automata_theory_to_database_systems
bridge_chains.description: From formal language theory through synchronization algorithms to distributed systems patterns. FSM convergence theory provides the mathematical foundation for sync-point discovery, which enables the speculative parallel decode validated by OCC-style commit protocols.

bridge_chains.name: information_theory_to_simd_engineering
bridge_chains.description: From information-theoretic stream interleaving through microarchitecture-aware parallelism to SIMD-accelerated reconstruction in a pipelined system. Each step addresses a different bottleneck: entropy decode throughput, instruction-level parallelism, memory copy bandwidth, and stage balancing.

bridge_chains.name: bit_manipulation_to_systems_engineering
bridge_chains.description: From low-level bit tricks through synchronization algorithms to full-system pipeline design. Bitvector operations accelerate the critical sync-finding step that enables stream splitting, which feeds into the pipelined decompression architecture.

bridge_chains.name: machine_learning_to_speculative_execution
bridge_chains.description: From learned statistical models through neural-inspired prediction to formal validation mechanisms. Block-level prediction bootstraps symbol-level speculation, validated by optimistic concurrency patterns grounded in automata-theoretic convergence guarantees.
